finding.claim: The /preview route fetches any URL the caller supplies. It has no scheme, host or IP validation. Redirects are followed by default. An unauthenticated attacker can make the server request internal services, loopback or cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. The first 500 characters of the response body and the status code are returned to the attacker, so this is a non-blind SSRF.
finding.source: request.args.get('url') at app.py:15 (query parameter 'url' on GET /preview)
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:16, with the response returned at app.py:17

trace.note: @app.route('/preview') registers the handler. There is no auth decorator or middleware anywhere in the app.
target = request.args.get('url', '') takes the attacker-controlled value unmodified.
requests.get(target) is called directly with that value.
resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] are returned to the caller, leaking internal responses.

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, no scheme check, no private or loopback IP filtering and no DNS pinning. The only control is timeout=5, which does not restrict the destination. allow_redirects is left at its default of True. The app has no auth, so any network client can reach the route.

verdict.reason: app.py:15 takes request.args["url"] and passes it straight to requests.get at app.py:16 with no host/scheme validation (unlike /partner at app.py:23-25), and app.py:17 returns the status and the first 500 body characters; the app has no auth, and app.py is the only file.
